used.how: took its fix 1 (trace the MoE half) and its prototype (capture after warm calls, bit-identical replay) as the design; checked its blocker list against the half (only P.56's guard and the planner's host state were in it)
a trace is captured only under MOE_PREV_HOST=device (the combine's fill args the same every call); legacy hands every call another ring slot and runs eager (TtMoEBlockMainLayer.trace_key)
capture only after eager calls of the same key (WARM=2): every program compiled, the block's lazy buffers, slots and the planner prepared before the capture
the traced half's input buffers (streams, ffn_hc's mixes) are allocated at load (moe_trace.prepare), never inside a forward
TtHcResidual._collapse hands on the given out / hc_out objects, not mhc_post's new wrappers, so the trace's input check (h is the buffer) holds
every model-level device run (quick probe, full measurement, diagnostic, measure, gate) started detached through devjob

contradicted.evidence: Its trace-blocker list calls 'allocations inside the capture' not a blocker; that holds only for its prototype (replays back to back, nothing eager between). With eager attention between replays, a DRAM buffer the capture allocated and freed is a hole a later allocation can take and the next replay overwrites; Metal warns 'Allocating device buffers is potentially unsafe due to the existence of an active trace' (tt_metal/impl/allocator/allocator.cpp:140). P.61 keeps every capture-time DRAM buffer allocated and checks it with a graph capture (tt/moe_trace.py _Keep / _holes, DS41-255). Also its 'P.56's guard' blocker is not one for a MoE-half trace: the guard stays a host decision outside the trace (pre_call). Its estimate '~93 ms host a chunk' for the MoE / FFN half: the half's own host time measured 51-56 ms (tests/test_moe_trace.py moe_host_ms, 40 layers), so the trace removed ~50 ms, not ~90.

missing: Metal drains the device before every trace replay (tt_metal/impl/trace/dispatch.cpp issue_trace_commands): ~46 us of idle a replay measured here; worth a perf_guide line next to the trace row
a trace's programs keep their capture-time runtime ids: the rt profiler's sections need the replay mapped (DS41-257)
with trace_region_size 0 the trace's command buffer goes top-down in DRAM (no device_params change needed)

overseer.evidence: no padding or duplicated work: the trace replays the same programs on the same buffers; the inputs are written in place by the producer (mhc_post output_tensor / hc_output), no copy
no Python-built op added or changed; the one in the half (P.56's planner, ttnn.bringup.run_prepared) stays prepared and is captured in the trace (its host launch ~95 us a call is gone on replays)
no fork regression or unit suite run; only the new tests/test_moe_trace.py (quick 4-layer, full 40-layer, one diagnostic pass) and the model-level measure / gate
